kept.title: Framework boot now fails completely when the per-user state dir or audit.db is unusable (CLI and GUI unusable)
kept.failure_scenario: FrameworkManager.initialize() now calls build_tool_registry(), which runs user_state_dir.mkdir and opens SQLite with `PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL` inside the boot try-block. Any OSError or sqlite3 error aborts the boot: a read-only or unwritable HOME (systemd ProtectHome, read-only containers), LLM_FRAMEWORK_HOME on an unmounted path, a corrupt ~/.llm-framework/audit.db, or a filesystem where WAL locking fails (NFS home). Every CLI command that boots the framework (build start/status, deploy, secrets, ...) then prints 'Failed to initialize framework', and the GUI shows 'Framework initialization failed' and exits. Before this change these commands worked, and registry.py itself says auditing must never break a call.
kept.evidence: With HOME pointing below a regular file: ab3367a `llm-cli -q build status` -> 'No builds found', exit 0. 84393cf -> CRITICAL 'Fatal Error during framework initialization: [Errno 20] Not a directory ... .llm-framework' raised from build_tool_registry (framework_tools.py:124), exit 1. With 4 KiB of random bytes as $LLM_FRAMEWORK_HOME/audit.db: 'sqlite3.DatabaseError: file is not a database' -> 'Failed to initialize framework', exit 1. main_window.py L84-86 calls sys.exit(1) when initialize() returns False.
kept.suggested_fix: Build the tool registry outside the fatal path: wrap build_tool_registry, and the AuditLog creation in particular, in try/except. On failure, fall back to a registry without audit, or with an in-memory audit and a logged warning, or set tool_registry=None so that only the tools, mcp and ditto commands report the problem. Open the database lazily on the first record().
kept.verify_reason: Reproduced. (1) With HOME below a regular file, `-q build status` at 84393cf fails with NotADirectoryError from user_state_dir.mkdir via build_tool_registry, printing 'Failed to initialize framework' and exiting 1. ab3367a prints 'No builds found' and exits 0. (2) With 4 KiB of random bytes in ~/.llm-framework/audit.db, 84393cf fails with sqlite3.DatabaseError 'file is not a database' from AuditLog.__init__ -> _connect (PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL), exit 1; ab3367a exits 0. build_tool_registry runs inside FrameworkManager.initialize's try block, so any exception returns False. The CLI's require_framework then calls sys.exit(1), and MainWindow shows 'Framework initialization failed' and calls sys.exit(1).
kept.corrected_fix: Wrap the creation of AuditLog/PolicyStore in build_tool_registry, or the build_tool_registry call itself, in try/except. On failure, log a warning and fall back to an audit sink that stays disabled or in memory, or set tool_registry=None so that only the tools, mcp and ditto commands report the problem. Better still, open SQLite lazily in AuditLog.record/verify and catch sqlite3/OSError there, as registry.py intends for auditing.

kept.title: A cancel during the security scan (or between stages) is overwritten, and the conversion still runs to completion
kept.failure_scenario: cancel_build() only sets progress.status=CANCELLED and stops the container in _active_containers. If the cancel arrives while _scan_image_security runs (a trivy container through containers.run, not tracked; minutes on a first run while it downloads its DB), _generate_imatrix (L751, status=CALIBRATING) or _execute_build_modules (L806, status=BUILDING) then overwrites CANCELLED before _run_container's _check_cancelled runs. The conversion container starts and the build ends COMPLETED. Meanwhile LLMOrchestrator.cancel_request has marked the request CANCELLED and cancelled the pipeline task. MCP/CLI/GUI report 'cancelled' while Docker keeps converting for possibly hours. cancel_request then returns False for that request, so it cannot be cancelled again.
kept.evidence: repro_cancel.py (fake Docker client, stubbed slow scan): `cancel_build -> True status: cancelled`, then `conversion container started after cancel: True` and `final engine status: completed`. There is no _check_cancelled between the scan (L446) and the status assignments at L751 and L806.
kept.suggested_fix: Never overwrite CANCELLED. Call self._check_cancelled(prog) after _scan_image_security and at the start of _generate_imatrix and _execute_build_modules, before any status assignment, or set the status under self._lock only when it is not CANCELLED. Track the trivy container in _active_containers so cancel_build can stop it.
kept.verify_reason: Reproduced with the real BuildEngine and a fake Docker client (verify-regressions/vr/repro_cancel_scan.py). The build entered the trivy containers.run, which is not tracked in _active_containers, and cancel_build there returned True with status 'cancelled'. Afterwards the container events were [('start','llm-build-b1')], the final status was 'completed' and a second cancel_build returned False. _execute_build has no _check_cancelled after _scan_image_security. _execute_build_modules (L806) and _generate_imatrix (L751) set status unconditionally before _run_container's _check_cancelled runs. On the orchestrator side, cancel_request has already set the request to CANCELLED and cancelled the task. _process_next_item's finally then pops _active_tasks, so a second cancel_request returns False. ab3367a was also broken here, but this change set rewrote cancellation, claims it keeps CANCELLED and exposes it as an MCP tool, so the defect is left broken by this change.
kept.corrected_fix: Call self._check_cancelled(prog) after _scan_image_security and at the top of _generate_imatrix and _execute_build_modules, before any status assignment. Better, add a helper that sets the stage status under self._lock only when the status is not CANCELLED, and use it for every stage assignment, including cleanup_build's CLEANING. Track or stop the trivy container: use containers.create plus _run_container instead of containers.run, so cancel_build can stop it.

kept.title: The audit HMAC key lives in the CWD-dependent config dir but audit.db is per-user, causing false tamper alarms; the MCP server started from a project uses different secrets and writes files into the project
kept.failure_scenario: _audit_key() stores 'audit_hmac_key' in SecretsManager's secrets.store under ConfigManager.config_dir. That dir is chosen from the working directory: CWD/configs, CWD/config, ~/.llm-framework, CWD. audit.db is always $LLM_FRAMEWORK_HOME or ~/.llm-framework/audit.db. Processes started from different directories therefore sign the same chain with different keys: the GUI or launcher from the install dir, and `llm-cli mcp serve` from Claude Code, which runs stdio servers in the project directory (the printed snippet sets no cwd). `llm-cli tools audit --verify` then reports 'Audit log was modified at entry N' with nothing tampered. The same CWD dependency gives the MCP server a different secrets store, so an hf_token set from the GUI or install dir is missing and gated-model builds started over MCP fail. On every boot the framework also writes secrets.store into a project's config/ folder and logs/audit.log into the CWD. A second process that saves secrets from a stale cache (SecretsManager._save_store rewrites the whole file) drops the key, so it is regenerated and the chain breaks again.
kept.evidence: repro_audit.py with a persistent file keyring: run from install/ -> config_dir=/install/configs verify=None; from proj/ -> config_dir=/home/.llm-framework verify=1; from install/ again -> verify=2. `secrets set hf_token` from install/, then `secrets list`: install/ shows audit_hmac_key and hf_token; proj/ shows only audit_hmac_key. A boot from a project with a config/ folder created proj/config/secrets.store and proj/logs/audit.log (ab3367a created neither).
kept.suggested_fix: Keep the audit key in the OS keyring (its own keyring entry) or in a 0600 file next to audit.db in user_state_dir, never in the CWD-dependent secrets store. Resolve the config dir for `mcp serve` against the installation path, or put cwd/--config into every client snippet, so the MCP server reads the same configs/secrets.store as the GUI and CLI. Also add `--cwd` or an explicit config path to the Claude Code command.
kept.verify_reason: Reproduced with a persistent file keyring (repro_audit_cwd.py). Run from the install tree: config_dir=<tree>/configs, verify=None. Run from a project dir: config_dir=~/.llm-framework, which always exists because user_state_dir creates it; verify=1. Run from the install tree again: verify=2. Each process signs the same per-user audit.db with a different audit_hmac_key from a different secrets.store. SecretsManager.secrets_file is config_dir/secrets.store, and ConfigManager._detect_config_directory depends on the CWD. The claude-code snippet sets no cwd (desktop and VS Code do), so the Claude Code MCP server reads a secrets store without the hf_token set from the GUI or install dir. Booting from a project with a config/ folder now also creates proj/config/secrets.store and proj/logs/audit.log, which ab3367a did not, because boot now calls get_secret/set_secret.
kept.corrected_fix: Store the audit key as its own OS keyring entry (e.g. keyring service 'llm-conversion-framework', user 'audit-hmac-key'). A 0600 file next to audit.db would defeat the HMAC, since anyone who can edit the db as that user can read the key. Make the MCP launch independent of the CWD. `claude mcp add` has no cwd setting, so add `-c <app_root>/configs` to launch_command's args for every client, or make ConfigManager prefer the installation path over Path.cwd().

kept.title: Relative `build start -o` paths are now resolved against the installation path instead of the user's working directory
kept.failure_scenario: A user in ~/work runs `llm-cli build start -m Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B -t Rockchip -o mybuilds`. The orchestrator now prefixes any relative output_base_dir with build_engine.base_dir (the install dir), so the build lands in <install>/mybuilds/Rockchip/... instead of ~/work/mybuilds, while the CLI panel shows 'Output: mybuilds'. On a Windows install (C:\Program Files\LLM-Conversion-Framework) a non-admin user gets a PermissionError. --dataset in the same command is still resolved against the CWD (cli.py L571), so the behaviour is inconsistent. `deploy list-artifacts` and `deploy package` (cli.py L938/L979) still read CWD-relative output/, so they do not find builds that now go to <install>/output when run outside the install dir.
kept.evidence: repro_outdir.py with a stub engine and cwd=/tmp/userproj_x, output_base_dir='mybuilds': the engine received '/.../review12/src/mybuilds/Rockchip/Qwen3.5-0.8B/Q4_K_M'. At ab3367a out_dir was Path(req.output_base_dir)/..., which is CWD-relative.
kept.suggested_fix: In the CLI, resolve a user-supplied --output-dir against the CWD (`str(Path(output_dir).resolve())`) before building the request. Keep the installation-path resolution only for the configured default output_dir. Use framework.resolve_path in the deploy commands as well.
kept.verify_reason: Reproduced with a stub engine (repro_outdir.py, cwd=a fresh user dir, output_base_dir='mybuilds'). ab3367a passed 'mybuilds/Rockchip/Qwen3.5-0.8B/Q4_K_M', which BuildEngine._extract_artifacts copied relative to the CWD. 84393cf passes '<install>/mybuilds/Rockchip/...'. The CLI hands a user-supplied -o through unresolved but resolves --dataset against the CWD (cli.py L571). deploy list-artifacts and deploy package (cli.py L938/L978-979) still use CWD-relative Path(ctx.config['output_dir']). Default builds (install/output) are therefore not found when the CLI runs outside the install dir. Before, both were CWD-relative and consistent. On Windows the install dir is Program Files (install.bat L41-42), which non-admin users cannot write to.
kept.corrected_fix: In start_build, resolve a user-supplied --output-dir with str(Path(output_dir).expanduser().resolve()) before building the request. Resolve the configured default with ctx.framework_manager.resolve_path(ctx.config['output_dir']). Use the same framework.resolve_path in deploy list-artifacts and deploy package.

kept.failure_scenario: `llm-cli build start -m X -t Rockchip -f rkllm -b RK3588` now exits 2 with "Unknown board 'RK3588' (known: rk3566, rk3568, rk3576, rk3588)". build.sh lower-cases TARGET_BOARD, so this was accepted before. target.yml's supported_boards and the docs list the boards in upper case. kept.suggested_fix: Normalize the board before validation (`board = board.lower() if board else None` in start_build), or make check_request compare case-insensitively, as BuildService.validate already does.

kept.title: `llm-cli mcp config` prints setup snippets that cannot be pasted: paths are unquoted and Rich panels hard-wrap them
kept.failure_scenario: client_snippets() builds `claude mcp add ... --env PYTHONPATH=<app_root> -- <sys.executable> -m ...` without shell quoting. On a Windows install (install.bat puts the code in C:\Program Files\LLM-Conversion-Framework) or any checkout path with a space, the command splits at the space and registers a broken server. The CLI also prints each snippet inside a Rich Panel (cli.py L922-925), which wraps long lines and adds '│' borders. Copying the command or the JSON from the terminal yields broken shell input or invalid JSON (strings split across lines).
kept.evidence: client_snippets(Path('/opt/LLM Framework'))['claude-code'] -> 'claude mcp add llm-cross-compiler --env PYTHONPATH=/opt/LLM Framework -- ...python -m orchestrator.cli -q mcp serve'. `COLUMNS=100 llm-cli -q mcp config` prints the command split over 4 boxed lines.
kept.suggested_fix: Quote with shlex.quote on POSIX and subprocess.list2cmdline on Windows. Print the snippets as plain text (console.print(..., soft_wrap=True) or print()) without a Panel, or offer `--write` for every client.
kept.verify_reason: Reproduced. client_snippets(Path('/opt/LLM Framework'))['claude-code'] yields '... --env PYTHONPATH=/opt/LLM Framework -- ...', and shlex.split gives ['PYTHONPATH=/opt/LLM', 'Framework', ...], which registers a broken server. install.bat installs to [ProgramFiles]\<AppName>, which contains a space, and sys.executable is the venv inside it. `COLUMNS=100 llm-cli -q mcp config` prints the command and the JSON hard-wrapped inside '│' borders, so copying them gives broken shell input or invalid JSON. Low severity, but the output is meant to be pasted.
kept.corrected_fix: Quote each argument: shlex.quote on POSIX; on Windows use subprocess.list2cmdline (cmd) or PowerShell-style quoting. Print the snippets without a Panel, e.g. plain print() or console.print(..., soft_wrap=True, markup=False) with a separate title line. Optionally add --write for vscode and claude-code.

kept.title: After a self-healing retry, read_build_log loses the failed attempt's log and shows the retry's log twice
kept.failure_scenario: _heal_and_retry calls _run_job again with the same job, so BuildConfiguration.build_id is the same. BuildEngine.build_model replaces self._builds[build_id] (builder.py L293), and _run_job appends the id to state.build_ids again. BuildService.log_tail iterates build_ids and returns the same BuildProgress logs twice, while the first attempt's log, which contains the failure that was healed, is gone. An MCP client or user calling read_build_log sees duplicated lines and cannot inspect the original failure. cancel_request also calls cancel_build twice for that id.
kept.evidence: repro_logdup.py (stub engine fails once, healer approves a retry): build_ids ['req_..._001', 'req_..._001']; read_build_log lines ['attempt 2: line A', 'attempt 2: line B', 'attempt 2: line A', 'attempt 2: line B'], none from attempt 1. Suite check for this review: 328 tests pass on Python 3.11, 3.12 and 3.14, in reversed order, with two shuffles and file by file, and test_mcp_server/test_foundation pass 3 repeated runs; no flaky or order-dependent tests. actionlint is clean. Only QtCore/QtGui/QtWidgets are imported, so pyside6-essentials is sufficient. The install.sh/install.bat 3.11-3.14 checks are correct.
kept.suggested_fix: Give each attempt its own build id (e.g. f"{job.job_id}_r{attempt}"), or skip appending an id that is already in state.build_ids and keep the earlier BuildProgress (e.g. store attempts separately) so the failed attempt's log stays readable.
kept.verify_reason: Reproduced with the real BuildEngine (stubbed stages: the first image build fails, the healer approves a retry) and BuildService.log_tail (repro_logdup.py). build_ids was ['req_..._001', 'req_..._001'] and the log contained only 'attempt 2' lines, twice; the 'attempt 1 ... Killed' lines that triggered healing were gone. _heal_and_retry reruns _run_job with the same job, and _map_job_to_config uses build_id=job.job_id. BuildEngine.build_model replaces self._builds[build_id] with a fresh BuildProgress, and _run_job appends the id again.
kept.corrected_fix: Give each attempt its own build id (e.g. f"{job.job_id}_r{n}" for retries), so both BuildProgress objects and their logs survive. At minimum, do not append an id already in state.build_ids, and keep the previous attempt's logs before reusing the id.

refuted.title: Each --write run overwrites the single .bak, so the user's original config is lost after a second run
refuted.reason: The mechanism reproduces: after a second run the .bak holds the already-modified file. But this is the usual single-rolling-backup behaviour, as in sed -i.bak and most installers, not a defect. Every other entry is kept in the main file on every run, as the commit promises. The only thing that can be lost is a previous 'llm-cross-compiler' entry, which the documented command replaces on purpose, and only after the user ran it twice. Timestamped backups or a --force prompt are a feature request.

refuted.title: CLI Ctrl+C does not cancel the build: the process blocks until the stage container finishes, while claiming the build is cancelled
refuted.reason: This bug predates the change set and the range does not touch it. The KeyboardInterrupt handler, including the exact message 'Interrupted; the build is cancelled when the CLI exits.' and sys.exit(130), is identical at ab3367a (cli.py:607-609), and the non-daemon ThreadPoolExecutor in BuildEngine is unchanged, so the exit-time join of the build thread happened before as well. The only related change, e9b7b5c routing Ctrl+C at the healing prompt into this handler, cannot cause the hang. That prompt only appears in AWAITING_APPROVAL, after the single CLI build job has already FAILED, so no stage container or build thread is running then. The underlying issue is real but pre-existing; the fix would be to call loop.run_until_complete(ctx.orchestrator.cancel_request(request_id)) before exiting.

refuted.title: Model path check resolves symlinks before testing the suffix, so a symlinked model file is refused
refuted.reason: The new check refuses nothing that could ever have been built. _stage_model, which this range does not change, also calls local.resolve() and mounts the blob under its hash name (/build-cache/input-model/<sha>). rknn_module.sh then dies with 'RKNN needs an ONNX model', because it requires *.onnx; GGUF and RKLLM need a model directory anyway. A symlink whose target has a model suffix passes, and symlinked directories pass via config.json. The early refusal therefore replaces a late failure after the image build. The confusing '<sha> is not a model file' wording is a message nit, and the staging limitation predates the range.

refuted.title: IMatrix is accepted for GGUF types that build.sh converts directly (F16/BF16/F32/Q8_0): the imatrix pass is wasted and the manifest wrongly says imatrix was used
refuted.reason: This behaviour predates the range and the range did not change it. At ab3367a the builder already ran _generate_imatrix whenever use_imatrix was set with a GGUF target and a dataset, for any quantization (old builder.py ~396-399). The manifest already wrote "imatrix": bool(config.use_imatrix and config.target_format == ModelFormat.GGUF) (old line 849; it is an unchanged context line in the diff). build.sh, whose GGUF_CONVERT_TYPES path ignores USE_IMATRIX, is not touched in the range; only target.yml changed under targets/. Before the range there was no validation, so F16+IMatrix was accepted then too. The model-card change in e9b7b5c reads the same manifest value, which is identical to the old config.use_imatrix result for GGUF. The new validator matches its own data (gguf imatrix: true). The waste and the wrong flag come from code this range did not change.
